{
  "residence_time_min": 60.0,
  "flow_rate_mL_min": 0.2,
  "temperature_C": 60.0,
  "concentration_M": 0.1,
  "BPR_bar": 8.0,
  "reactor_type": "PFA tubular coil flow reactor with a low-holdup PFA static micromixer, two independently heated zones, outlet cooler, and corrosion-compatible back-pressure regulator",
  "tubing_material": "PFA for all wetted reactor tubing and mixer components; avoid unqualified elastomers and copper/brass components",
  "tubing_ID_mm": 1.0,
  "reactor_volume_mL": 12.0,
  "residence_time_basis": "Liquid-phase hydraulic residence time from the mixed-feed reactor inlet to the reactor outlet, before downstream dilution/quench. Calculated as 12.0 mL divided by 0.200 mL/min. No intentional gas is used.",
  "residence_time_inlet_min": 60.0,
  "residence_time_in_channel_min": 60.0,
  "light_setup": "None; thermal nitration only",
  "wavelength_nm": null,
  "streams": [
    {
      "stream_label": "A",
      "pump_role": "Substrate feed",
      "contents": "Aniline derivative, 0.100 M",
      "solvent": "S_batch, defined as the industrial batch solvent. Numerical starting example assumes glacial acetic acid only if it is confirmed to be the batch solvent and compatible with the substrate and nitric acid.",
      "phase": "liquid",
      "flow_rate_mL_min": 0.1,
      "concentration_M": 0.1,
      "molar_equiv": 1.0,
      "gas_flow_sccm": null,
      "gas_flow_actual_mL_min": null
    },
    {
      "stream_label": "B",
      "pump_role": "Nitrating reagent and acid feed",
      "contents": "Nitric acid, 0.240 M, equivalent to 2.40 equiv versus substrate; prepared by controlled dilution of qualified nitric acid stock into S_batch under cooling",
      "solvent": "S_batch; use the same solvent and water specification as the validated batch process",
      "phase": "liquid",
      "flow_rate_mL_min": 0.1,
      "concentration_M": 0.24,
      "molar_equiv": 2.4,
      "gas_flow_sccm": null,
      "gas_flow_actual_mL_min": null
    },
    {
      "stream_label": "C",
      "pump_role": "Post-reactor dilution/quench feed",
      "contents": "Cold deionized water for controlled dilution of residual nitric acid before collection; neutralization is performed separately after confirming temperature and gas evolution are controlled",
      "solvent": "water",
      "phase": "liquid",
      "flow_rate_mL_min": 1.0,
      "concentration_M": null,
      "molar_equiv": null,
      "gas_flow_sccm": null,
      "gas_flow_actual_mL_min": null
    }
  ],
  "mixer_type": "Low-holdup PFA interdigital or split-and-recombine static micromixer, followed by approximately 0.4 mL of 1.0 mm-ID PFA tubing as the initial temperature-controlled reaction segment",
  "mixing_order_reasoning": "Meter streams A and B simultaneously into the micromixer; do not add concentrated nitric acid into a stagnant substrate reservoir. Simultaneous, high-shear mixing limits localized excess nitric acid, suppresses hot spots, and makes the exothermic nitration heat load continuously removable. Stream C is introduced only after the 12.0 mL reaction coil to avoid changing the specified reaction residence time or prematurely quenching nitration.",
  "pre_reactor_steps": [
    "Confirm the identity, water content, acid compatibility, and maximum safe operating temperature of S_batch before implementation; the batch solvent was not specified in the source protocol.",
    "Perform reaction calorimetry or a small-scale flow thermal-screening experiment with the actual substrate, nitric acid concentration, and S_batch before operating at 60 C.",
    "Prepare Stream B by adding nitric acid stock slowly to cooled S_batch with external cooling; never prepare the acid feed by adding organic substrate to concentrated nitric acid.",
    "Filter both feeds through chemically compatible filters if solids are present, and verify pump calibration gravimetrically.",
    "Prime the reactor with S_batch at ambient temperature, pressure-test with solvent, and establish 8 bar back pressure before introducing nitric acid.",
    "Start Stream A and Stream B at 20-25 C, confirm stable total flow of 0.200 mL/min, then apply the staged reactor temperature profile."
  ],
  "post_reactor_steps": [
    "Cool the reactor effluent to 20 C or below before dilution.",
    "Introduce Stream C immediately downstream of the cooler through a second PFA mixer; maintain a closed, vented-to-scrubber collection system.",
    "Pass diluted effluent through the 8 bar BPR into a shielded receiver connected to an alkaline NOx/acid scrubber.",
    "Analyze collected material by HPLC or UPLC for starting material, mononitrated intermediates, dinitrated product, and oxidation/decomposition products before changing flow rate or temperature.",
    "After analytical confirmation and cooling, neutralize residual acid slowly in a separately engineered quench vessel; account for possible heat release and NOx evolution.",
    "Perform phase separation, extraction, washing, and product isolation according to the validated batch workup rather than assuming the reported 89% batch yield transfers directly."
  ],
  "chemistry_notes": [
    "The reported batch procedure does not identify the aniline derivative, nitric acid concentration, nitric acid equivalents, industrial solvent, water content, or product regiochemistry. The proposed 2.40 equiv nitric acid is a starting assumption for dinitration, not a confirmed optimum.",
    "A 60 minute flow residence time is intentionally conservative relative to typical intensified-flow nitrations and should first be evaluated at low throughput. It is shorter than the 4 hour batch hold but is not expected to be equivalent without analytical validation.",
    "The proposed substrate throughput is 0.0100 mmol/min, or 0.600 mmol/h. Nitric acid delivery is 0.0240 mmol/min.",
    "Aniline derivatives can undergo protonation, oxidation, tar formation, and altered regioselectivity under strongly nitrating conditions. Product ratio and yield must be measured rather than inferred from the 89% batch result.",
    "If S_batch is not compatible with nitric acid dilution, is biphasic, precipitates the substrate/product, or has unacceptable thermal behavior, this design must be re-engineered rather than substituted with an arbitrary solvent."
  ],
  "stage_parameters": {
    "feed_temperature_C": 20.0,
    "total_reaction_flow_mL_min": 0.2,
    "stage_1": {
      "purpose": "Controlled initiation and heat removal after mixing",
      "temperature_C": 35.0,
      "volume_mL": 0.4,
      "residence_time_min": 2.0
    },
    "stage_2": {
      "purpose": "Thermal nitration hold",
      "temperature_C": 60.0,
      "volume_mL": 11.6,
      "residence_time_min": 58.0
    },
    "reactor_total": {
      "volume_mL": 12.0,
      "residence_time_min": 60.0,
      "calculation": "12.0 mL / 0.200 mL/min = 60.0 min"
    },
    "post_reactor_dilution": {
      "cooler_outlet_temperature_target_C": 20.0,
      "water_flow_mL_min": 1.0,
      "combined_flow_to_BPR_mL_min": 1.2
    },
    "approximate_coil_length_m": 15.3
  },
  "reasoning_per_field": {
    "residence_time_min": "A 60 minute initial residence time provides a conservative starting point for a reaction that required 4 hours in batch, while retaining a practical 12 mL flow reactor size. It is a screening condition, not a claim of kinetic equivalence.",
    "flow_rate_mL_min": "Equal 0.100 mL/min liquid feeds give a simple total reactor flow of 0.200 mL/min and support accurate low-throughput safety evaluation.",
    "temperature_C": "The principal reaction zone is maintained at the reported 60 C batch temperature; a short 35 C entrance zone reduces the risk from the initial exotherm.",
    "concentration_M": "0.100 M substrate is a deliberately diluted initial condition intended to reduce heat release and fouling risk. It should not be considered the unidentified industrial batch concentration.",
    "BPR_bar": "An 8 bar BPR maintains a liquid-filled reactor, provides stable flow, and reduces flashing risk. Its wetted materials must be verified for hot nitric-acid service.",
    "reactor_type": "A small-ID PFA coil and static mixer provide high heat-transfer area, low reactive inventory, and continuous removal of product from strongly acidic conditions.",
    "tubing_material": "PFA is selected as a conservative wetted material for nitric-acid-containing feeds; compatibility must still be verified for temperature, acid strength, and the actual solvent.",
    "tubing_ID_mm": "A 1.0 mm ID gives manageable pressure drop at 0.200 mL/min and good radial heat transfer for an exothermic nitration.",
    "reactor_volume_mL": "The 12.0 mL volume exactly matches the specified 60.0 minute residence time at 0.200 mL/min.",
    "light_setup": "No photochemical reagent or irradiation was specified in the batch protocol.",
    "streams": "Separate substrate and nitric-acid feeds prevent prolonged storage of the complete reactive mixture and allow rapid shutdown by stopping either pump.",
    "mixer_type": "A low-holdup static micromixer minimizes local acid concentration gradients without requiring moving parts in corrosive service.",
    "pre_reactor_steps": "The missing solvent and reagent-strength information are critical process-safety variables, so compatibility and calorimetric confirmation precede the proposed operating point.",
    "post_reactor_steps": "Cooling and controlled dilution reduce the hazard of handling acidic, potentially NOx-forming effluent; separate neutralization avoids uncontrolled gas evolution in the reactor train."
  },
  "literature_analogies": [
    "Continuous-flow aromatic nitrations are commonly designed with separate substrate and nitrating-agent feeds, low-holdup mixers, heat-transfer-efficient tubular reactors, and downstream quench/dilution because nitration reactions can be strongly exothermic.",
    "Two-zone flow reactors are commonly used for fast exothermic reaction initiation followed by a longer isothermal conversion segment.",
    "These are general process-design analogies only; no direct literature precedent for the unspecified aniline derivative, industrial solvent, or claimed dinitration selectivity has been established from the supplied protocol."
  ],
  "engine_validated": false,
  "safety_flags": [
    {
      "flag": "Exothermic nitration and thermal-runaway risk",
      "control": "Use low substrate concentration, low holdup volume, staged heating, independent temperature sensors at mixer outlet and reactor outlet, automatic pump shutdown on high temperature or pressure, and pre-run calorimetry."
    },
    {
      "flag": "Nitric acid is strongly corrosive and oxidizing",
      "control": "Use qualified PFA wetted components, chemically compatible pump heads/seals, secondary containment, face shield and acid PPE, and documented material-compatibility testing."
    },
    {
      "flag": "Potential NOx generation",
      "control": "Operate as a closed system with a pressure-rated receiver vented to an appropriate alkaline NOx/acid scrubber; do not vent reactor effluent directly to the laboratory."
    },
    {
      "flag": "Blockage or precipitation risk",
      "control": "Confirm solubility of substrate, intermediates, and dinitrated product at all feed compositions and temperatures; monitor pressure differential and install a shielded relief path."
    },
    {
      "flag": "Unknown batch solvent and nitric acid strength",
      "control": "Do not run this as a production condition until the actual industrial solvent, water content, nitric acid assay, and substrate identity have been supplied and assessed."
    },
    {
      "flag": "Quench hazard",
      "control": "Cool before dilution, add quench solvent continuously, and perform neutralization only in a separately controlled vessel sized for heat and possible gas evolution."
    }
  ],
  "confidence": {
    "overall": "low-to-moderate",
    "basis": "The hydraulic design and arithmetic are internally consistent, but the chemistry-specific operating window is uncertain because the substrate identity, nitric acid strength/equivalents, industrial solvent, water content, and batch workup were not provided.",
    "required_validation": [
      "Confirm feed stability and solubility.",
      "Perform calorimetry/thermal screening with actual feeds.",
      "Run an ambient-temperature compatibility test.",
      "Increase temperature from 35 C to 60 C only with online pressure and temperature monitoring.",
      "Quantify conversion, dinitration selectivity, and impurity profile by HPLC/UPLC before optimization."
    ]
  }
}
